meta.title: Player dossier
meta.honesty: Selections come from published match-day 23s. Points and tries come from the Test score sheets in data/all-blacks-2026.json. Injuries come from All Blacks, RNZ, ESPN and Planet Rugby. Nothing on this page is a rating, a prediction, or a guess at minutes.
meta.checked: On 12 October 2026 the Rugby Database games list had one new game after Baltimore: Eden Park, All Blacks 50-19 Australia, on 10 October. The ESPN match page shows the same score. Sydney on 17 October is not on the Rugby Database list and had not been played.
meta.next: Saturday 17 October, Australia, Accor Stadium, Sydney. The kick-off is not verified. Eden Park on 10 October is played: New Zealand 50–19 Australia.
meta.recordLine: Tests: played 8, won 5, lost 3. Eden Park was won 50–19. South Africa won that series 3–1. Tour matches are on the main page and are not in the player charts.
meta.captain: Codie Taylor captained Eden Park and the Bledisloe squad named 29 September 2026. Ardie Savea captained the Tests he started, through Soweto.
meta.scoringNote: Try 5, conversion 2, penalty goal 3. A penalty try is 7 and is not given to a player. Charts use the eight Tests only.
meta.sheetNote: Start and bench mean the player was named in that match-day 23. It is not a minute count.
meta.squadNote: 34 players were named on 29 September. On 11 October four did not travel to Sydney and four replacements were added. The travelling group is still described as a squad. A fresh head count was not published as a new number.

tests.note: Anton Segner was in the first named bench. SABC Sport reported he was replaced by Simon Parker before kick-off. Parker is the bench loose forward used here.
Ethan de Groot and Josh Lord were left out. The team announcement said both were still in concussion protocols.
Ardie Savea, Luke Jacobson and Quinn Tupaea were ruled out injured. Fabian Holland was unavailable with illness. Codie Taylor captained.
Codie Taylor captained. Damian McKenzie started at first five and Beauden Barrett at fullback. BBC's reserve list prints Loane. The All Blacks sheet and Rugby Database say Rieko Ioane.

learnings.title: Eden Park was won after a tight first half
learnings.text: New Zealand 50–19 Australia. Half-time 17–14. Seven tries to three. The tries were Peter Lakai, Tupou Vaa'i, Cam Roigard, Codie Taylor, Leroy Carter, Josh Moorby and Will Jordan. Damian McKenzie kicked six conversions and one penalty. Sky and BBC both have five of the seven tries after the break. On 1News, Rennie said the first half was an arm wrestle and that opportunities were left out there, then that the areas which needed to be better after South Africa showed shifts. An ESPN story quoted him on mindset, work rate and brutality.

learnings.title: The high ball, the review item after South Africa, was the thing Rennie praised
learnings.text: On 1News, Rennie said Cam Roigard's kicking was excellent, that they kicked more off nine than they had been, and that receiving those kicks is difficult. He said the players did an excellent job of winning the ball in the air or picking up the scraps. Les Kiss, in an ESPN story, said New Zealand won the aerial battle and credited Roigard's kicking. This is the coach's reading of one Test. It is not a contest count.

learnings.title: The win cost four players for Sydney
learnings.text: The All Blacks injury update on 11 October named four players who will not travel. Leroy Carter, high ankle sprain, suffered while scoring. Asafo Aumua and Anton Segner each failed a second head-injury assessment and have a minimum 12-day stand-down. Ethan Blackadder injured a calf in the warm-up and was not in the 23. The replacements travelling are Anton Lienert-Brown, George Bell, Du'Plessis Kirifi and Jamie Hannah. Scott Barrett failed an assessment on the night and passed a second one. He travelled. Use the injury list for who is actually available. Do not brief Sydney as the Eden Park 23.

learnings.title: Ellis Park is the pattern that worked against this Springboks side
learnings.text: The only win of the series was 33–16 at Emirates Airline Park on 22 August. New Zealand scored five tries to one: Will Jordan two, Josh Moorby, Fabian Holland and Luke Jacobson. Ruben Love kicked four conversions and no penalties. Half-time was 12–13, so the lead was built after the break. The All Blacks site, reviewing the series, said the attack can trouble the Springboks. This is the match that showed it. It was the last win of the South Africa series. The next win was Eden Park, against Australia, on 10 October.

learnings.title: Points took too long, and South Africa punished the mistakes
learnings.text: The All Blacks site said the attack can trouble the Springboks, but New Zealand too often needed long passages of possession to score. In Baltimore, Will Jordan's try finished a patient 32-phase attack. The same report said South Africa were more ruthless after penalties and turnovers. Cape Town was 14–24 at half-time and finished 26–33. Soweto was 12–12 at half-time and finished 24–29, with a penalty try to South Africa. Baltimore finished 28–43. The series was lost 1–3 after the Ellis Park win.

learnings.title: Needless penalties are the points the forwards can stop giving away
learnings.text: After Baltimore, Dave Rennie said needless penalties have to come out of the game, and he called that sort of penalty dumb. The All Blacks site said South Africa were more clinical with the chances they created, especially after penalties and turnovers. The Soweto score sheet includes a penalty try to South Africa. That is seven points with no kicker. ESPN's series review counted 14 scrum penalties conceded, including one penalty try, and a lineout at 86 percent after eight lost throws. Those series counts are ESPN's. They are not re-counted from a second feed here.

learnings.title: The Baltimore set piece was the one Rennie was happy with. The series was not that consistent.
learnings.text: Rennie said the scrum and lineout in Baltimore were excellent. Across the series, the All Blacks site still named set-piece consistency as a review area. Use Baltimore as the picture of the set piece they want, and the ESPN penalty count above as the picture of what leaked in the other Tests. Do not treat the ESPN count as an official All Blacks statistic.

learnings.title: The loose-forward meeting is about replacing Savea and Jacobson, not about a new system
learnings.text: Savea started the first six Tests at No. 8 and captained them. He scored once at Cape Town and twice at Soweto before leaving the field. Jacobson started all six of those Tests at openside and scored at Ellis Park. Both missed Eden Park. The Eden Park loose forwards were Tupou Vaa'i at blindside, Peter Lakai at openside and Wallace Sititi at No. 8, with Shannon Frizell and Anton Segner on the bench. Lakai and Vaa'i scored. Segner then failed a head-injury assessment and does not travel to Sydney. Du'Plessis Kirifi was called in. Ethan Blackadder hurt a calf in the warm-up and also stays home. Codie Taylor captained.

learnings.title: The high ball is still the back-three review
learnings.text: After Baltimore, Rennie said the high ball put the side under more heat and that they could not take a lot of those balls. The All Blacks site listed collection of contested kicks as a review area. ESPN wrote that Will Jordan had a series-high 24 high-ball turnovers. That 24 is ESPN's count. It is not on the score sheets and it is not re-counted here. The cue for the back three is the contested kick, not a new attacking shape.

learnings.title: Smaller wingers defending in midfield were moved off the ball
learnings.text: ESPN's series review said Leroy Carter and Josh Moorby, stationed in midfield, were pushed off the ball and that this led to three tries. Both are in the Bledisloe squad. Caleb Clarke, the power wing, is out with a shoulder tendon injury. The meeting point is a defensive one: if Carter or Moorby is in the 13 channel, the collision beside him has to be planned. The three tries are ESPN's reading of the series. They are not listed try-by-try on this page. That note is about the South Africa series. At Eden Park, Carter started on the wing, scored, and then suffered a high ankle sprain that rules him out of Sydney. Moorby came off the bench and scored.

learnings.title: Eden Park was McKenzie at 10 and Beauden Barrett at fullback
learnings.text: Ruben Love started the first six Tests at first five and is out for the rest of the season. Richie Mo'unga started Baltimore, then missed Eden Park with a calf strain and is likely to miss Sydney. Damian McKenzie, who had started the first seven Tests at fullback, started at first five and kicked 15 points. Beauden Barrett started at fullback. Josh Jacomb is still uncapped in these sheets. The All Blacks selection story said McKenzie had been training at first five, and that Barrett's most recent games had been at fullback.

learnings.title: Counter-attack was the plan in July. These sheets do not show whether the tries came that way.
learnings.text: Before the July Tests, Rennie said he treats counter-attack as a set piece because so much possession arrives from kicks, and that he wanted more tries from counter-attack and turnover ball than the year before. The score sheets list who scored. They do not list the phase. So the plan is on the record, and the 42 Test tries are on the record. How many of those 42 started from a kick return is not verified.

learnings.title: The July block was three wins. It is not a six-from-six season.
learnings.text: France 34–32, Italy 47–17, Ireland 40–21, then the Ellis Park win, then three losses. The four tour matches were also wins, and they are not Tests.
